column2: Before politics she studied chemistry at Oxford and worked as a research chemist, testing emulsifiers for a food company. It's such a pub-quiz staple that plenty of people know it.

In 1916 he dipped his pen into molten tin instead of his inkwell and pulled out a thin metal thread, a single crystal. His method now grows the silicon crystals that almost every computer chip is cut from.

At 23 he invented the electrolysis that still makes almost all the world's aluminium, in 1886, the same year as Charles Martin Hall in America. The two rivals were born in the same year, 1863, and died in the same year, 1914.
A pharmacist who in 1912 devised a way to rate chilli heat using a panel of tasters. Everyone who's eaten a hot wing knows his scale, so it's not the obscure answer it sounds.
Before politics she had a doctorate in quantum chemistry and worked as a research chemist in East Berlin.
